asA: operator observing long-running scheduled work on a Worker
iWant: the dispatcher to fire cronStalled at the moment a handler's observed duration crosses the elicited soft budget, without terminating the handler
soThat: the applied logging companion surfaces stalled fires as a first-class signal, and the Worker's own CPU budget remains the vendor's concern

acceptanceCriteria.description: With softBudgetMs=100 and a spy handler that resolves after 250ms of fake-clock time, dispatching fires exactly one cronStalled event on the sink with {expression, scheduledTime, outcome: stalled, duration: >=100, softBudgetMs: 100} at the moment the observed duration crosses 100ms.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a dispatcher configured with softBudgetMs=100 and a spy handler that resolves after 250ms fake-clock
acceptanceCriteria.then: a cronStalled event fires exactly once with the observed duration at or past the budget

acceptanceCriteria.description: With softBudgetMs=100 and a spy handler that resolves after 250ms of fake-clock time, the dispatcher does NOT terminate the handler on the soft-budget breach; the handler runs to completion, resolves, and a final cronFired event follows the cronStalled record with the total duration.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a dispatcher configured with softBudgetMs=100 and a spy handler that resolves after 250ms fake-clock
acceptanceCriteria.then: the handler runs to completion and a cronFired follows the cronStalled record

title: T-2 soft budget: a handler running past the elicited budget logs cronStalled and continues
